newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH plans drinks merger with Guinness, GrandMet.
newsitem.headline: LVMH plans drinks merger with Guinness, GrandMet.

text.p: LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton on Wednesday unveiled a plan for merging its drinks activities with those of British groups Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan.

In a statement, LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault said he had sent a proposal to the two companies today for a merger of the Moet Hennessy cognac and champagne business with United Distillers of Guinness and International Distillers & Vitners of GrandMet to create a group that would have had sales of 7.4 billion stg ($12.4 billion) for the year 1995/96.
The new company would be quoted in London and Paris.

LVMH said it would have a stake of about 35 percent in the new drinks and spirits group in exchange for its 66 percent stake in Moet Hennessy -- in which Guinness holds the remainder -- and its 12.4 percent stake in Guinness as well as a 6.4 percent stake in GrandMet.
Existing shareholders in Guinness and GrandMet would get shares in the new company as well as shares of three separately listed companies for food, fast-food and brewing.
In addition, the shareholders would get 60 pence each for their shares in Guinness or GrandMet.
LVMH said that under its plan the existing merger proposal by Guinness and GrandMet -- called GMG Brands and unveiled in May -- would be adjusted to include Moet Hennessy.

LVMH added that if its plan was adopted, arbitrage concerning a buyout of Guinness's stakes in joint-ventures of the two companies as well as the 34 percent in Moet Hennessy would be dropped. LVMH was claiming that the May merger plan was a "control event" which allowed it to buy back the stakes from Guinness at a discount.
